recognize_zh: 低倍骨髓抹片細胞極多，大部分是中至大型、核染色質細緻、有核仁、細胞質量中等偏藍的母細胞（箭頭），正常成熟顆粒球與紅血球前驅細胞明顯被取代，符合急性骨髓性白血病。
features: Markedly cellular aspirate dominated by medium-to-large blasts
Blasts with round to slightly irregular nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and one or more nucleoli
Moderate amount of pale-to-moderately basophilic cytoplasm, some with fine azurophilic granules
Residual maturing neutrophils, eosinophil precursors and scattered orthochromatic normoblasts
No Auer rods clearly resolved at this magnification
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at low power is markedly cellular and shows a predominance of medium-to-large blasts with finely dispersed chromatin, visible nucleoli and moderate basophilic cytoplasm, some containing fine granules (arrow). Residual granulocytic maturation, eosinophil precursors and scattered erythroid precursors are present but reduced. Auer rods cannot be confidently assessed at this magnification. A blast count on a 500-cell differential, cytochemistry/flow cytometry and genetic studies are needed for classification. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts are typically smaller with scant agranular cytoplasm and are MPO-negative/TdT-positive, whereas these blasts have more cytoplasm and some granules.
BPDCN blasts often show gray-blue agranular cytoplasm with peripheral vacuoles and pseudopods and are CD4/CD56/CD123/TCL1-positive and MPO-negative.
MDS has fewer than 20% blasts with prominent multilineage dysplasia, rather than sheets of blasts replacing the marrow.
Recovery marrow shows a synchronous wave of promyelocytes and myelocytes with orderly maturation, not a dominant population of agranular blasts.
